$comment: no-environment: ok — the standard, not a network
title: home.yml — a house, for La Régie (schema 1)
description: The contract every house writes to. Things are data: an id, a room, a kind, how it is reached. Packs add fields to a thing (their schema fragment is merged before validation); kinds and via are OPEN vocabularies — an unknown value is a warning, never an error, so a new use case is a pack, not a schema bump.

schema.description: the schema version this file is written to; `regie migrate` moves a file forward

name.description: an id for the house (paths, topics)

url.description: the brain's URL for the phones (internal and external are the same door)

my.description: My Home Assistant (my.home-assistant.io): true = Home Assistant's default, every OAuth consent redirects through the project's page; false = the brain's own door is the callback (<url>/auth/external/callback - what a vendor's app registers) and default_config is rendered explicitly without `my`

profile.description: where the brain runs: a folder under profiles/ (ct, and later pi, vm, docker)

packs.description: the use cases enabled: product packs (packs/) and the house's own (paths.house_packs)

root.description: the brain's tree on its host; the profile's default otherwise

house_packs.description: a directory of the house's own packs, relative to home.yml

units_dir.description: where the host's units go (`regie up`); the profile's default otherwise

owner.description: the brain's own owner account — the break-glass login that needs no provider; its password is the secret `owner_password`. Created by `regie apply` at the first boot (Home Assistant's onboarding), never by a person at a screen.

backup.description: Home Assistant's own backup, scheduled by `regie apply` (encrypted with the secret `backup_password`)

time.description: local time of the nightly backup

tokens.description: long-lived access tokens the house's own machines need (a scraper, an automation that calls the API) — minted once by `regie apply`, kept root-only under <root>/.regie/tokens/<name>, never printed

floors.description: the floors the areas name (optional: a floor an area names without a line here is created with its id as its name)

pins.description: the images' tags; the profile carries the versions this release was tested against, a house may override (doctor says so)

proxy.description: a reverse proxy in front of the brain (optional)

trusted.description: its addresses or networks (X-Forwarded-For is trusted from these)

via.description: the proxy's address the brain proves its door through before promoting the HTTP config (default: the one trusted proxy when it is a single host) - on the brain the door's name may resolve to the brain itself

oidc.description: an OpenID Connect door (optional — without it, Home Assistant's own login). The client secret is the secret `oidc_client_secret`.

admin.description: the provider's group that makes an admin

user.description: the provider's group that lets a person in

features.description: the component's `features:` block, passed as is (automatic_person_creation, include_groups_scope, default_redirect, ...)

claims.description: the component's `claims:` block, passed as is (display_name, username, groups)

channel.description: fixed before the first pairing; changing it re-pairs the mesh

host.description: where the things reach the broker; the brain itself uses the loopback

level.description: 0 = the ground floor; the UI sorts by it

coordinator.description: one Zigbee radio = one Zigbee2MQTT instance; reached over TCP. Its address comes from the thing it names (kind: coordinator) or from `host`.

thing.description: the thing (kind: coordinator) whose `host` is the radio's address

host.description: the radio's address, when it is not a thing

adapter.description: zstack (TI CC26x2), ember (Silicon Labs), deconz, zigate, zboss

base_topic.description: the instance's MQTT root; `zigbee2mqtt` for the first coordinator, `zigbee2mqtt_<id>` for the others

id.description: one name, three systems: the Zigbee2MQTT friendly name, the MQTT topic, the entity's object id

kind.description: what it is (x-known.kinds + the packs'); open

via.description: how it is reached (x-known.via + the packs'); open

label.description: the family's word for this one; the kind's label otherwise

ieee.description: a Zigbee thing's address — filled by the pairing walk

coordinator.description: the radio a Zigbee thing is on; the first coordinator otherwise

mac.description: a network thing's hardware address (a reservation, a row)

entity.description: the entity id when it cannot be derived from the kind and the id

integration.description: the Home Assistant integration(s) that reach it — one config entry each (the conductor's business); a list when one box is several things to Home Assistant (a receiver: heos + denonavr; a TV: androidtv_remote + cast)

bind.description: a control bound inside the mesh to things or areas (an area = its Zigbee group)

options.description: what a pack reads on a thing of its kinds; each pack documents its own
